"name": "exonum-client",
  "version": "0.18.4",
  "scripts": {
    "test": "cross-env BABEL_ENV=test grunt test",
    "proto": "pbjs --keep-case -t static-module -p proto proto/exonum/*.proto proto/exonum/**/*.proto -o ./proto/protocol.js",
    "proto:test": "pbjs --keep-case -t static-module -r tests -p proto test/sources/proto/*.proto -o ./test/sources/proto/stubs.js",
    "proto:integration-tests": "pbjs --keep-case -t static-module -r tests -p proto integration-tests/src/proto/*.proto -o ./integration-tests/src/proto/stubs.js",
    "integration:build": "cargo build --manifest-path integration-tests/Cargo.toml",
    "integration": "npm run proto:integration-tests && cross-env BABEL_ENV=test mocha -r @babel/register integration-tests/test.js",
    "preintegration:unix": "npm run integration:build && npm run postintegration:unix && cargo run --manifest-path integration-tests/Cargo.toml & sleep 10",
    "integration:unix": "npm run proto:integration-tests && cross-env BABEL_ENV=test mocha -r @babel/register integration-tests/test.js",
    "postintegration:unix": "lsof -iTCP -sTCP:LISTEN -n -P 2>/dev/null | awk '{ if ($9 ~ /:8000$/) { print $2 } }' | xargs -r kill -KILL",
    "coveralls": "cross-env NODE_ENV=test nyc mocha ./test/sources/*.js && cat ./coverage/lcov.info | coveralls",
    "prepare": "npm run proto && npm run proto:test && grunt compile",
    "lint": "eslint ./src ./test ./examples",
    "lint:fix": "npm run lint -- --fix",
    "git-publish": "npm run prepare && . ./git-publish.sh"
  },
slice_results.behavior_summary: During installation, the npm prepare script executes protobuf compilation commands (pbjs) to generate static JavaScript modules from .proto files and runs a Grunt compile task, facilitating the preparation of protocol buffer definitions for use in the package.
slice_results.explanation: [LLM Judgment: Benign] The provided code snippet defines npm scripts primarily for protobuf compilation (pbjs) and testing/building integration tests. Unlike the known malicious patterns, it does not execute native code compilation (e.g., node-gyp), nor does it run obscure or deeply nested JavaScript files during install or preinstall phases. The scripts are standard development and build tasks without any indication of obfuscation, hidden payloads, or system manipulation. The prepare script runs protobuf generation and grunt compile, which are legitimate build steps. There is no evidence of suspicious behavior such as executing native code, running hidden scripts, or network/system manipulation that matches the known malicious patterns.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: This is suspicious because the dependency name 'axios' is widely trusted, but the source is a remote tarball for a different, obscure package. This misleads both users and automated security tools, and can be used to introduce malicious code into the dependency tree without detection.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: Normally, specifying 'axios' as a dependency would cause npm to fetch the official, vetted 'axios' package from the npm registry. malice_analysis.similar_legitimate_use: Legitimate use of remote tarballs in dependencies is rare and typically only seen for private/internal packages or urgent hotfixes, never for public packages masquerading as popular libraries. Using a popular package name to fetch a different package is not a legitimate practice.

package.json lacks legitimate metadata or documentation

This pollutes the npm ecosystem, undermines trust in dependency resolution, and creates a vector for potential supply chain attacks if the remote tarball is weaponized.

attack_chain.leads_to: npm resolves dependencies and, due to the crafted package.json, fetches the remote tarball for '@putrifransiska/kwonthol36' instead of the real 'axios' package.

seed = rdrand()
csprng = strong_init(seed)
